audience: Accounting users who need to know which vendors Odoo owes the most, for example before a payment run or a month-end review.
goal: Produce the exact list of **vendors ranked by credit value**: open **Journal Items**, keep only the **Payable** lines, group them by **Partner**, then sort by the **Credit** column so the largest vendor credits come to the top.
before: **Developer mode is on.** The **Journal Items** menu entry is only listed in developer mode (see step 3 for how to switch it on).
Your journal entries are **posted** — draft entries are not included in this ranking.
outcome: A list with **one row per vendor**, showing that vendor's total **Debit** and **Credit**.
The vendors with the **highest credit** are at the top of the list.
notes: The screenshots were captured on a **test database** with developer mode switched on (the small bug icon and database name in the top bar). Vendor names and amounts are test data and will differ from yours.
The red banner at the top of the screenshots ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases.

phases.title: Open Journal Items
phases.summary: Go to the full list of accounting entry lines.
phases.checkpoint: The **Journal Items** list is open and shows every accounting entry line.

phases.title: Keep vendor lines and total them per vendor
phases.summary: Filter to Payable lines, then group by Partner so each vendor becomes one row.
phases.checkpoint: The search box shows **Payable** and **Partner**, and the list has one row per vendor.

phases.title: Rank the vendors by credit
phases.summary: Sort by the Credit column, twice, so the biggest credits are at the top.
phases.checkpoint: The vendor with the **highest credit** is at the top of the list.

glossary.meaning: The full list of accounting entry lines — every debit and credit that has been recorded, from every journal.
A filter that keeps only the lines on payable accounts, i.e. what you owe to vendors.
The company or person an entry belongs to — here, the vendor.
Collapses the list into one row per value (here per vendor) and shows the totals of the columns for that row.

The two sides of every entry. On a payable account a vendor bill adds to the **Credit** and a payment shows as a **Debit**, so the Credit total reflects how much has been recorded as owed to that vendor.
An extra Odoo mode that shows technical menus and options, including Journal Items. Switch it on by adding **?debug=1** to the address (for example `…/odoo?debug=1`), or from the Settings page.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
1.see: The Accounting app opens, with its menu bar across the top (Dashboard, Customers, Vendors, Accounting, Reporting …).
1.tip: If your menu bar shows fewer items than the list above, widen the browser window — the remaining items hide behind a **+** at the right end of the bar.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen (the grid of app icons).
Find the **Accounting** icon.
Click it.

2.title: Open the Accounting menu
2.do: In the top menu bar, click **Accounting**.
2.see: A drop-down opens with the groups Miscellaneous, Journals, Ledgers, Management and Actions.
actions: Look along the top menu bar for **Accounting**.
Click it to open its drop-down.

3.title: Open Journal Items
3.see: The Journal Items list opens, showing every accounting entry line.
3.warning: If **Journal Items** is not in the menu, developer mode is off. Add **?debug=1** to the address (for example `…/odoo?debug=1`), reload the page, and open the menu again.
3.tip: Do not click **Purchases** by mistake — it is a different view, with its own filters and grouping.
3.where: Accounting app > Accounting > Miscellaneous > Journal Items
actions: In the drop-down, look at the **Miscellaneous** group at the top.
Click **Journal Items**.
If you cannot see it, switch on developer mode first (see the warning below).

4.title: Open the Filters / Group By panel
4.do: Click the small **down-arrow** at the right end of the search box to open the **Filters / Group By** panel.
4.see: A panel opens with three columns: **Filters**, **Group By** and **Favorites**.
4.tip: You will use the Filters column in the next step and the Group By column in the one after.
4.where: Journal Items list > search box > down-arrow
actions: Find the search box at the top of the list.
Click the small **down-arrow** at its right-hand end.
A panel with **Filters**, **Group By** and **Favorites** opens.

5.title: Filter to Payable lines
5.see: A **Payable** filter appears in the search box, next to **Posted**. The list now shows only vendor payable lines.
5.tip: **Posted** is applied by default, so only posted entries are counted.
actions: In the **Filters** column (left), find **Payable**.
Click it.
A **Payable** tag appears in the search box.

6.title: Group the lines by Partner
6.see: The list collapses into **one row per vendor**, with the number of entry lines in brackets and the vendor's total Debit and Credit.
6.warning: Make sure **Partner** is the only grouping. If another grouping such as **Journal Entry** is also ticked, untick it — otherwise each vendor is split up by entry instead of shown as one total.
actions: In the **Group By** column (middle), find **Partner**.
Click it.
Check that **Partner** is the only ticked grouping.

7.title: Sort by Credit (first click)
7.do: Close the panel by clicking anywhere outside it, then click the **Credit** column header **once**.
7.see: An arrow appears on the **Credit** header and the vendors are sorted by credit, **smallest first** — you will see many vendors with a credit of 0.00 at the top.
7.tip: This first click sorts from the smallest value to the largest. You want the opposite, which is the next step.
7.where: Journal Items list > Credit column heading
actions: Click anywhere outside the search panel to close it.
Find the **Credit** column heading.
Click it **once**.
An arrow appears — vendors are now sorted with the smallest credit first.

8.title: Sort by Credit again (second click)
8.do: Click the **Credit** column header **a second time**.
8.see: The arrow flips and the vendors with the **highest credit** move to the top of the list. That is your ranking.
8.tip: Open a vendor row (click its name) to see the individual entry lines behind its total. A row called **None** is not a vendor — it groups the entry lines that have no partner set.
8.where: Journal Items list > Credit column heading
actions: Click the **Credit** heading a second time.
The arrow flips.
The vendors with the largest credit move to the top.
